transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for having me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. 

I just... well, I came in because I've been having this sort of silly problem, and I hope it's okay to bring it up. I just feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It's hard to explain, but... even when I am just completely worn out and I know I really should be sitting still, I get this feeling like I just have to jump up and do the next thing. 

It makes me feel a bit foolish at my age, to be honest, not being able to just relax like a normal person. Am I explaining that right? Is that the sort of thing you help people with?
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications—especially antipsychotics, anti-nausea drugs, or antidepressants—in the weeks before this restlessness began?

Oh, no, I haven't. I'm sorry, I hope that's the right answer... but no, I haven't started anything new or changed any doses lately. I just take my regular vitamins, really. I haven't been on any of those kinds of medicines you mentioned. Is that okay? I mean, I hope I'm not making this harder to figure out by not having a medication to point to.

When you feel this need to get up and move, is it usually accompanied by worried or anxious thoughts running through your mind, or does it feel more like just a physical urge to move without any particular worries attached?

Oh, um, let me think... no, I don't think it's worry. I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression, but I'm not really sitting there fretting over things. I try very hard not to be a worrywart, you know? 

It's really just... well, it's more like my body itself just wants to go. Just this physical pull to get up and be doing something. I don't really have a bunch of anxious thoughts going around in my head when it happens, just that feeling in my bones. 

Is... is that the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out.
Does this restless feeling specifically involve an urge to move your legs, and does getting up and moving around make it feel better?

Oh, um... no, it's not just my legs. I mean, my legs do feel it, but it's kind of... everywhere? Like my whole self just needs to be doing something. And, well, I guess getting up and moving around does help a little bit, but... it doesn't really make it go away completely. I just end up bouncing from one little task to another. 

I hope that makes sense? I know you asked about my legs specifically, and I'm sorry if I'm not giving a very clear 'yes' or 'no'. I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so I don't lead you down the wrong path. Am I doing okay?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed a persistent low or sad mood, or a loss of interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Oh, um, no... no, I haven't been feeling sad or anything like that. I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? I don't want to be a burden or a downer to anyone. 

I still like doing my usual things, even if I get a little... distracted while doing them. But I definitely haven't lost interest. I still enjoy my days. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that symptom either? I know you're trying to put all these pieces together, and I really hope I'm being helpful and not just giving you a bunch of 'nos'. Am I giving you the right kind of information?
Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss, feeling unusually hot or sweaty, a racing heartbeat, or trembling hands along with this restlessness?

Oh, um, no... no, I haven't noticed anything like that. My weight is pretty much the same, and I don't think I've been extra sweaty or had a racing heart. And my hands are pretty steady, I think. 

I really try to take good care of my health, you know? I go for walks when I can, even if I get a little sidetracked. I just... I don't want you to think I'm falling apart physically or anything. 

Is it... is it bad that I don't have those things either? I feel like you keep asking about all these other problems and I just keep saying no. I really am trying my best to give you good answers. Are we still on the right track?
Can you tell me approximately how long you've been experiencing this restless, need-to-move feeling—has it been going on for weeks, months, or even since you were younger?

Oh, well... I mean, I've always been a little busy, you know? Always doing things around the house. But... this really restless feeling, where it's actually causing trouble... I'd say that really started about, um, a year and ten months ago. 

That's... that's when my husband passed away. I've just been trying to keep things together since then, you know? Not let the house fall apart or anything. I don't want anyone to think I'm not coping well. 

I hope that answers your question? I know it's a bit specific, but I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline. Is that the kind of detail you need?
Since your husband passed away, do you find yourself frequently longing for him or having him on your mind most of the day, even now?

Oh, um... well... I mean, of course I miss him. We were together a long time. But... no, I wouldn't say I spend most of the day longing for him or anything like that. 

I really try to stay busy and focus on what needs to be done. I don't want to just sit around dwelling on the past, you know? I feel like he would want me to keep moving forward and taking care of things. So, I just... I try to keep my thoughts on the present, mostly. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I didn't care about him! I did, very much. I just... I try to be strong about it. Is that... is that a normal way to handle things? I just want to make sure I'm dealing with it the right way.

Would you say this restless feeling has actually interfered with your daily activities, sleep, or relationships, or is it more just an uncomfortable feeling that hasn't really stopped you from doing what you need to do?

Oh... well... I try really hard not to let it get in the way, I really do. I want to be able to handle everything myself. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it has been causing some trouble. 

My family... they've actually had to step in recently to help me with the bills and some of the paperwork. And... oh, this is so hard to admit, but the people at my church, and my garden club... they've had to redo some plans or cover responsibilities that I just... I sort of dropped. 

I feel so embarrassed about it. I really care about those groups, and it just breaks my heart to think they might feel like they can't count on me anymore. I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible, like I'm just letting everyone down. I really am trying my best to stay on top of things, I promise. Is it... is it okay that I've had to lean on them a little bit? I just want to make sure I'm not failing completely.

Since it started almost two years ago, has this restless feeling been pretty constant the whole time, or does it come and go—getting worse on certain days, like anniversaries or when something reminds you of your husband?

Oh, um... well, it's... it's pretty constant, I suppose. I mean, I try not to let it be, but... it's just always sort of there, humming in the background, if that makes sense? 

It's not really tied to anniversaries or... or anything like that. I really do try to keep a positive outlook and not dwell on the sad things. It's just this... this constant need to be doing something, every single day. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too... I don't know, scattered? I really am trying to keep it under control. Does that make sense, though? That it's just sort of an everyday thing, rather than being triggered by memories? I want to be sure I'm explaining it right.
Since this restless feeling started, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep or waking up during the night?

Oh, um... my sleep? Well... I try to get a good night's rest, I really do. I know how important it is to be well-rested so I can tackle the day and not be a burden on anyone. 

But... no, I wouldn't say I've noticed any big changes, really. I mean, everyone has a restless night now and then, right? It's nothing out of the ordinary. I usually just try to close my eyes and, you know, hope for the best. 

I don't think the restless feeling has made it any worse. At least, I hope it hasn't. Is it... is it normal that my sleep hasn't really changed much? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I'm trying to be as helpful as I can!
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, activities, or reminders of your husband because they're too painful, or do you still have trouble accepting that he's really gone?

Oh, no, no... I wouldn't say I do that. I mean, of course I miss him terribly, but I really try to be strong about it. I don't want to be one of those people who just completely falls apart and makes everyone else uncomfortable, you know? 

I still go to all our usual spots, and I try to keep his memory alive in a... in a positive way. I know he's gone, I really do. I try to accept it with grace, so I don't worry my family. 

I'm not avoiding things or... or living in denial. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm handling it the right way, the way I'm supposed to. I'm really trying my best to move forward like everyone says I should. Does that sound like I'm coping alright?
Do you think staying constantly busy and active helps keep your mind off thoughts or feelings about your husband's death?

Oh, um... well, I suppose you could say that. I mean, I do keep quite busy, but I don't want you to think I'm running away from anything. I just... I like to be useful, you know? 

Most days I just sort of... well, I move from the garden, and then maybe over to the senior center, and then there are always errands for the church, and then I come home and sort through papers... all without really taking a breath. It's just... I feel like if I stop, everything might just fall apart. 

But I'm not doing it to avoid thinking about him, I promise. I just want to be productive and not sit around feeling sorry for myself. I hope that's the right way to handle things? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing. Is it okay that I keep that busy?

When something forces you to stop and just sit quietly for a while, do you notice any inner tension, unease, or distress building up, or does it just feel like a physical urge to move without any emotional discomfort?

Oh, um... well, I try to just be peaceful when I have to sit. I really do. I don't want to be a bother or seem fussy. But... I suppose, if I'm being perfectly honest... that's actually sort of why I finally came in to see you. 

I just feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It's... it's like I have to jump up and do the next thing, even when I'm just completely worn out and I know I really should be sitting still. I try so hard to just relax like everyone else does, but it's very difficult. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too... difficult or anxious. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question properly. Is it normal to feel that way when you're just trying to rest?

When you're finally forced to sit still and can't distract yourself with tasks, do you notice any emotional discomfort—like sadness, guilt, or unease—coming up underneath the physical restlessness, or is it truly just a physical need to move with no emotional feelings attached?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say it's sadness or guilt or anything like that. I really try not to let myself wallow, you know? I want to be strong. 

It's really just... it's just this physical feeling. Like my legs just need to get up and go, and my hands need to be doing something. It's not that I'm sitting there crying or feeling sorry for myself, I promise. It's just... I just feel so fidgety and restless, like a motor is running inside me that I can't turn off. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm hiding my feelings or anything. I just... I don't feel sad when I sit still, I just feel like I absolutely have to move. Is that alright? Does that make sense to you?

Doctor: I understand. That physical restlessness, that feeling of a motor running—has that always been there, even when you were younger, or is it something that started more recently, perhaps around the time your husband passed away?

Patient: Oh, well... um, I've always been a bit of a busy bee, I suppose. Even when I was a little girl, my mother used to say I was her little helper because I was always buzzing around doing something. 

So, yes, I think that feeling of needing to be on the go has always been a part of me. It's not just since... since he passed. I've always had a hard time just sitting and watching television or doing nothing. I always needed to be knitting or folding laundry or... something. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound like a nuisance, being so restless all my life. I always just thought of it as having good energy, you know? Is it okay that I've always been this way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.

Compared to how you were before your husband passed away, would you say this restless feeling has become noticeably more intense or harder to control since then, or does it feel about the same as your usual energetic self?

Well, um... I suppose it has gotten a bit harder to manage lately. I always tried to keep it under control so I wouldn't bother anyone, but... if I'm being completely honest, it's been causing real trouble for me since he passed away. That was about... oh, a year and ten months ago now. 

I just... I don't want you to think I'm falling apart or not handling things well. I really am trying my best to keep busy and be productive. But since he's been gone, that buzzing feeling is just so much stronger, and I just can't seem to get a handle on it like I used to. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound weak or... or like I'm not coping properly. It's just been a bit of a struggle recently. Is it understandable that it would get worse after something like that? I just hope I'm explaining it right.
Since your husband passed, have you noticed any sense that part of your own identity or sense of self died with him, or that life feels empty or meaningless without him?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, of course I miss him terribly, but I really try to keep my chin up. I don't want to be one of those people who just gives up on life, you know? 

I still have my routines and my chores, and I try to keep everything nice and tidy just like always. I don't feel like my life is completely empty... I just have to find new ways to fill the time, I suppose. I really do try to stay positive and keep moving forward. 

I hope that's the right way to handle it. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself or that I've lost who I am. I'm still me, just... trying to adjust. Does that sound like a normal way to be feeling?

Oh, my... um, I'm not entirely sure I know what you mean by that. I haven't really noticed anything like that, no. 

I hope that's an alright answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know, and I don't want to be unhelpful. I try to be very observant about how I'm doing, but... no, not that I can think of. Is it okay that I don't have a better answer for you? I can try to think on it a bit more if you need me to.
Since your husband passed away, have you noticed any feelings of anger, bitterness, or guilt connected to his death or the circumstances surrounding it?

Oh, no, no... nothing like that. I really don't have any anger or bitterness about it. It was his time, and... well, I just try to accept it as peacefully as I can. 

And guilt? Oh, I hope I don't give the impression that I feel guilty. I did everything I could to make him comfortable, and I really tried to be a good wife to him right up to the end. I don't want to sound like I'm holding onto negative feelings or being resentful. I think it's so important to be gracious about these things, don't you? 

I just want to be sure I'm answering this the right way... is it normal to not feel angry about it? I just try to focus on the good years we had, and I hope that's a healthy way to look at it.

patient.answer:
Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for having me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this.
